issues.what: The family SPA p-values (1 min 0.396, 5 min 0.4965) are still inflated by a near-duplicate of the benchmark inside the 1,568-variant family, and the follow-up's statement that no such variant exists is false. Variant 1177 (stop foundation / no target / no trail / CHoCH-against on) reproduces the Foundation L1 exit on all but 8 of 4,452 one-minute trades and all but 1 of 826 five-minute trades (variant 1183 likewise on 5 min): the CHoCH-against cut IS the engine's next-CHoCH exit (same bar on 99.8%, same close price on 100%). Its selection-gain vector is 'non-zero in every session' only because the variant net is lab.price_trade's unrounded value while the label l1_net_inr is rounded to 2 dp (|gain| <= 0.0049 INR in 571 of 578 sessions), so harness.spa's exclusion rule (threshold 1e-9) excludes nothing and the revised harness is a no-op on this family. That variant is the argmax of the SPA bootstrap null statistic in 396 of 2,000 draws (1 min) and 758 of 2,000 (5 min, together with 1183). Removing the near-duplicates moves the studentised SPA p from 0.396 to 0.322 (1 min) and from 0.4965 to 0.185 (5 min). The pass rule still fails (both > 0.10), so the null verdict stands, but a headline multiplicity statistic is materially wrong on 5 min and the FINDINGS explains the zero exclusions with an incorrect fact.

L1 next_choch exits: exit px == close of exit bar on 100%, exit bar == first CHoCH-against bar on 99.7%; l1_net_inr has > 2 decimals on 0 trades, grid nets on all trades.
issues.fix: In harness.spa define activity on a material tolerance (e.g. |gain| > 0.01 INR, or count units where |kept - benchmark| > 0.005) or round the variant nets to 2 dp as the label is before building the vectors; rerun H.spa for both timeframes and report the studentised p with the near-duplicates excluded (expected ~0.32 / ~0.19) beside the current numbers; rewrite FINDINGS 10.2 to state that the family contains a benchmark duplicate (variants 1177 / 1183) and that the exclusion rule as coded did not catch it; the verdict (no candidate) is unchanged.

issues.what: The only other failing pass-rule item on 1 min, 'diff with the top 1% of per-trade gains removed > 0', uses a metric variant that (a) was fixed after learner C's results had been read (the script's own docstring) and (b) is mechanically negative-biased: removing the 45 largest values of a difference distribution with this dispersion lowers the mean by 154 INR even when the difference has zero mean, so 'gains removed' can only pass when the mean gain exceeds ~154. The harness's pre-registered definition (GO diff_top1_removed: remove the top 1% winners by net) corresponds to the study's own diff_top1_winners_removed, which is positive for every 1-min learner (nested +4.01, B +18.57, IS best +22.83) and would PASS. The qualitative statement that the +87 is carried by the top 1% of trades is nevertheless correct (the 45 trades contribute +153.4/trade of the +86.6 mean; the other 4,407 trades net -66.8), and the verdict still fails on SPA, so this does not change the null; but one of the two decisive FAIL items rests on a post-hoc, stricter metric choice that is not disclosed as such in the pass-rule text.

The verdict 'no candidate on either timeframe' survives every variant I tried: SPA with the near-duplicates excluded (0.322 / 0.185), unstudentised SPA (0.5405 / 0.1505), trade-weighted SPA (0.3455 / 0.7515), the harness-definition top-1% item (passes on 1 min but SPA still fails), and learner A (worse than C and B on 1 min, hurts on 5 min). A stop-floored random control I tried was discarded as invalid (it conditions on the stop bar, a look-ahead), so the study's no-stop control is the right causal one even though it is weak (Foundation itself scores 97).
